cvm_fetch(): the generic API

Source: vignettes/articles/issuer-fetch.Rmd
issuer-fetch.Rmd

cvm_fetch(dataset, table, ...) is the single entry point for every CVM dataset and every table covered by the package.

This article walks through each argument: how issuers are selected (cnpj, ticker), how the period is selected (year or from/to), the basis rule for financial statements, the validate and on_error modes, and the cache/source plumbing.

issuer_fetch(), the entry point of v0.1 and v0.2, is deprecated: it still works, with a lifecycle warning, and will be removed in a later release. Its issuer argument (CNPJ, CD_CVM, free text or ticker) and report_type map onto the arguments described here.

library(cvmdata)

Anatomy 

cvm_fetch(
  dataset,
  table,
  cnpj     = NULL,
  ticker   = NULL,
  year     = NULL,
  from     = NULL,
  to       = NULL,
  basis    = NULL,
  source   = NULL,
  on_error = "abort",
  validate = "strict",
  ...
)

Returns a tibble of subclass cvm_tbl carrying seven provenance attributes (source, fetched_at, group, dataset, table, package_version, release). Column names, table names and categorical values are preserved in Portuguese as published by CVM; the API surface is in English.

bb_bpa <- cvm_fetch(
  "dfp", "bpa",
  cnpj = "00.000.000/0001-91",
  year = 2024,
  basis = "ind"
)
#> duckdb keeps downloaded extensions and secrets in a temporary directory:

Identifying issuers

cvm_fetch() identifies issuers by two keys only, and the two combine in a single call:

Argument Accepts Match against
cnpj CNPJ, with or without punctuation, vector of any length cnpj_cia / cnpj_companhia, punctuation stripped
ticker B3 trading code (PETR4, BBAS3, BBDC11) codigo_negociacao in fca/valor_mobiliario, resolved to the issuer’s CNPJ

A CVM code ("1023") or a company name ("BCO BRASIL") passed as cnpj aborts with cvmdata_error_input: there is no free-text search and no CD_CVM lookup in cvm_fetch(). To find the CNPJ of a company you know by name or by CVM code, read the registry, which carries cd_cvm, denom_social and cnpj_cia side by side:

registry <- cvm_fetch("cad", "companhias")
#> duckdb keeps downloaded extensions and secrets in a temporary directory:
#> ℹ /tmp/RtmpiN7Slb/duckdb
#> This is removed when the R session ends.
#> • Extensions are re-downloaded each session.
#> • Secrets are lost.
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = TRUE) (or create ~/.duckdb) to keep them (suitable for most users).
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = FALSE) to accept the temporary directory (and silence this message).
#> ℹ See ?duckdb_storage for details and alternatives.
registry[grepl("MAGAZINE LUIZA", registry$denom_social),
         c("cd_cvm", "denom_social", "cnpj_cia")]
#> ℹ source: "mirror" | release: "mirror-companhias-cad-latest" | fetched_at:
#>   2026-10-25 17:52:01.386781
#> ℹ group: "companhias" | dataset: "cad" | table: "companhias"
#> # A tibble: 1 × 3
#>   cd_cvm denom_social      cnpj_cia          
#>   <chr>  <chr>             <chr>             
#> 1 22470  MAGAZINE LUIZA SA 47.960.950/0001-21

A CNPJ absent from the table yields zero rows for it, silently — a miss on a taxpayer id is not a typo the package can second-guess.

Ticker: resolved through the registration form

A B3 trading code is looked up in fca/valor_mobiliario (read from the same source as the data), and the issuer’s CNPJ is then filtered exactly as cnpj would be. The lookup reads every yearly FCA file that carries trading codes (2018 onwards; the column is empty in earlier files), so the code of a company that has since left the exchange still resolves, for any year: GOLL4 fetches Gol’s statements of 2019 although the company cancelled its registration in 2026. Tickers cover only exchange-listed securities; a code absent from every file aborts with cvmdata_error_input rather than returning an empty tibble, and so does a code that maps to more than one issuer (none does today; pass cnpj in that case).

petr <- cvm_fetch("dfp", "bpa", ticker = "PETR4",
                  year = 2024, basis = "con")

Selecting the period

Two mutually exclusive forms; passing both aborts.

Whole years with year

year is an integer vector of any length (singular naming follows tidyverse conventions), matching the yearly files the CVM publishes. NULL (default) fetches the latest available year, discovered by HEAD-probing CVM’s listing (or from the mirror’s inventory). Must be NULL for snapshot tables such as cad/companhias.

# What's published upstream?
cvm_dataset_years("dfp")
#>  [1] 2010 2011 2012 2013 2014 2015 2016 2017 2018 2019 2020 2021 2022 2023 2024
#> [16] 2025 2026

# Pass an explicit vector to back-fill history:
history <- cvm_fetch("dfp", "bpa", cnpj = "00.000.000/0001-91",
                     year = 2022:2024, basis = "ind")
#> duckdb keeps downloaded extensions and secrets in a temporary directory:
#> ℹ /tmp/RtmpiN7Slb/duckdb
#> This is removed when the R session ends.
#> • Extensions are re-downloaded each session.
#> • Secrets are lost.
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = TRUE) (or create ~/.duckdb) to keep them (suitable for most users).
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = FALSE) to accept the temporary directory (and silence this message).
#> ℹ See ?duckdb_storage for details and alternatives.
#> duckdb keeps downloaded extensions and secrets in a temporary directory:
#> ℹ /tmp/RtmpiN7Slb/duckdb
#> This is removed when the R session ends.
#> • Extensions are re-downloaded each session.
#> • Secrets are lost.
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = TRUE) (or create ~/.duckdb) to keep them (suitable for most users).
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = FALSE) to accept the temporary directory (and silence this message).
#> ℹ See ?duckdb_storage for details and alternatives.
sort(unique(format(history$dt_refer, "%Y")))
#> [1] "2022" "2023" "2024"

Each CSV publishes ORDEM_EXERC ∈ {ÚLTIMO, PENÚLTIMO} — the declared year and N − 1. The antepenultimate of year N is the last of year N − 2. cvm_fetch() does not synthesize the antepenultimate; ask for year = (N - 2):N if you need it. To read an exercise by its own year, with the figures originally filed and the comparative of the following year’s file labelled, see reading below.

table(history$ordem_exerc)
#> 
#> PENÚLTIMO    ÚLTIMO 
#>       144       144

A date window with from and to

For slices smaller than a year, pass from and to together as complete dates ("YYYY-MM-DD" strings or Date scalars). Rows are kept when the document’s reference date (dt_refer in CAD/ITR/DFP-style tables, data_referencia in FRE-style tables) falls inside the window; the yearly files actually read are the years the window spans. The reference date is the period the filing describes, not the day it was delivered.

# ITR balance sheets referenced in the first half of 2024
h1 <- cvm_fetch("itr", "bpa", cnpj = "00.000.000/0001-91",
                from = "2024-01-01", to = "2024-06-30",
                basis = "con")
#> duckdb keeps downloaded extensions and secrets in a temporary directory:
#> ℹ /tmp/RtmpiN7Slb/duckdb
#> This is removed when the R session ends.
#> • Extensions are re-downloaded each session.
#> • Secrets are lost.
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = TRUE) (or create ~/.duckdb) to keep them (suitable for most users).
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = FALSE) to accept the temporary directory (and silence this message).
#> ℹ See ?duckdb_storage for details and alternatives.
#> duckdb keeps downloaded extensions and secrets in a temporary directory:
#> ℹ /tmp/RtmpiN7Slb/duckdb
#> This is removed when the R session ends.
#> • Extensions are re-downloaded each session.
#> • Secrets are lost.
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = TRUE) (or create ~/.duckdb) to keep them (suitable for most users).
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = FALSE) to accept the temporary directory (and silence this message).
#> ℹ See ?duckdb_storage for details and alternatives.
unique(h1$dt_refer)
#> [1] "2024-03-31" "2024-06-30"

Incomplete dates ("2024", "2024-06") are rejected, as is a window on a snapshot table. One bound without the other aborts; for whole years use year.

Partial failure with on_error

When several yearly files are read (more than one element in year, or a window spanning several years), on_error = "warn" keeps surviving years and emits cvmdata_warn_partial_failure listing failures. on_error = "silent" does the same without the warning. on_error = "abort" (default) aborts at the first HTTP failure. Total failure (every year fails) always aborts regardless. Single-year calls, non-yearly tables (CAD) and the implicit year = NULL fallback always abort on HTTP failure.

Parse and schema-validation failures are governed by validate, not by on_error — schema drift is treated as a separate signal.

basis

Eight tables in ITR/DFP publish both individual and consolidated variants of the same concept (bpa, bpp, dre, dra, dfc_md, dfc_mi, dmpl, dva). basis is required for those, with no default: many issuers file only individual statements, so defaulting to "con" would silently drop them.

cvm_fetch("dfp", "bpa", cnpj = "00.000.000/0001-91", year = 2024)
#> Error in `check_basis()` at cvmdata/R/api-cvm-fetch.R:250:3:
#> ! Table "dfp"/"bpa" requires `basis`.
#> ℹ Pass `basis = "ind"` for individual statements, `basis = "con"` for
#>   consolidated, or `basis = c("ind", "con")` for both.

basis takes "ind", "con" or c("ind", "con"). With both, the two variants are read and stacked. Whatever you ask for, those eight tables always carry a basis column in the result, so a single value and a stacked pair have the same shape:

both <- cvm_fetch("dfp", "bpa", cnpj = "00.000.000/0001-91",
                  year = 2024, basis = c("ind", "con"))
#> duckdb keeps downloaded extensions and secrets in a temporary directory:

#> This is removed when the R session ends.

On every other table (companhias, submissao, parecer, composicao_capital, every FRE/FCA detail table) basis must be left unset; passing it aborts rather than being ignored:

cvm_fetch("dfp", "composicao_capital",
          cnpj = "00.000.000/0001-91", year = 2024,
          basis = "ind")
#> Error in `check_basis()` at cvmdata/R/api-cvm-fetch.R:250:3:
#> ! Table "dfp"/"composicao_capital" has no individual/consolidated split;
#>   leave `basis` unset.
#> ✖ Got "ind".

reading

The same eight tables carry two columns of figures per account in every yearly file: ordem_exerc = "ÚLTIMO", the exercise the file is about, and ordem_exerc = "PENÚLTIMO", the comparative the issuer presented for the previous exercise. That comparative is often restated — after a change of accounting policy, an error, a reorganisation — and it is the figure later statements build on. Measured on the DFP, about a third of the issuers restate: Porto Seguro’s consolidated total assets of 2022 are R$ 50.5 bn in the 2022 file and R$ 39.9 bn in the 2023 one.

reading reads an exercise by its own year and labels the two readings. "original" is the ÚLTIMO rows of the file of year; "restated" is the PENÚLTIMO rows of the file of year + 1, which the call reads on its own; c("original", "restated") stacks both. Rows come as published, with a reading column appended:

pssa <- cvm_fetch("dfp", "bpa", ticker = "PSSA3",
                  year = 2022, basis = "con",
                  reading = c("original", "restated"))

dt_refer and versao are those of the document each row came from (the restated row is dated 2023); dt_fim_exerc — and dt_ini_exerc in the flow statements — identify the exercise, so the two readings pair on the issuer, the exercise dates, cd_conta and, in dmpl, coluna_df. Either reading can be missing for an issuer that stopped or started filing between the two years, and the restated figure is whatever the issuer presented: the banks that adopted CMN Resolution 4,966 in 2025 presented no comparative for 2024 on the individual basis, and their restated reading of 2024 is a column of zeros, as in the CVM file.

An exercise whose following year’s file is not published yet has no restated reading; the call says so and returns what exists. When the file exists but the issuer has not filed in it yet (the current year’s file opens with the first non-December fiscal years), the restated rows are simply absent:

latest <- cvm_fetch("dfp", "bpa", ticker = "PSSA3", year = 2025,
                    basis = "con", reading = c("original", "restated"))

With from/to, the window applies to the exercise end (dt_fim_exerc) rather than to the document date, so an exercise’s two readings stay together. Without reading (the default) each file comes as the CVM publishes it, ÚLTIMO and PENÚLTIMO rows together, and there is no reading column. In the ITR, the comparative of the balance sheet (bpa, bpp) is the previous year end, not the previous year’s quarter, so the restated reading of an ITR balance sheet is the year-end balance as the following year’s quarterly filings present it; the flow statements (dre, dfc_*, dva, dmpl) compare like with like.

validate

Controls the strictness of schema validation at parse time. Three modes:

Mode Table with META published Table with meta_status: missing
"strict" Validates; mismatch aborts. Aborts with cvmdata_error_meta_unavailable.
"warn" Validates; mismatch warns. Warns with cvmdata_warn_meta_unavailable; data returned.
"skip" Skips validation silently. Skips silently.

The eight FRE tables without published META (empregado_PCD, empregado_local_declaracao_genero, etc.) need validate = "warn" or "skip" to be readable. See the fre article for a worked example.

Cache, TTL and source backend

Downloaded artefacts are cached under tools::R_user_dir("cvmdata", "cache"). Each ZIP / CSV stores an ETag/Last-Modified sidecar; HTTP revalidation is throttled by a 30-day TTL (configurable via options(cvmdata.cache_ttl_seconds)). Cached units are LRU-evicted once total size exceeds the limit set by options(cvmdata.cache_max_size_mb) (default 100 MiB).

info <- cvm_cache_info()
info
#> # A tibble: 0 × 8
#> # ℹ 8 variables: group <chr>, dataset <chr>, file <chr>, path <chr>,
#> #   size_bytes <int>, mtime <dttm>, etag <chr>, last_modified <chr>
attr(info, "total_size_bytes")
#> [1] 0

source selects the backend: from v0.1.0 the default is "mirror", which reads parquet snapshots from GitHub Releases via DuckDB with year-partition filter pushdown; "cvm" reads the open-data portal over HTTP and remains fully supported. The current backend is read by cvm_source_get() and changed at session scope by cvm_source_set():

cvm_source_get()
#> [1] "mirror"
